name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Crawford running with a large cash advantage
Democrat Terri Green raised only $65k with $12k on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~98%
model.rationale: Crawford is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 23 points, while Green has raised almost nothing and lacks cash on hand. Markets price a Republican win at roughly 98%, and no polling or expert ratings suggest any reason to move away from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise outside-spending surge for Green or an unexpected Crawford scandal would be the only realistic path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Crawford seeks another term in this heavily Republican northeastern Arkansas district, which has a partisan lean of 23 points toward the GOP. He enters the general election with over $1 million on hand after raising more than $940,000. Democrat Terri Green has raised only about $65,000 and had under $12,000 on hand as of the latest filings, leaving her with little capacity to communicate with voters. A Libertarian candidate, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot but has no reported fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98% chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong Republican lean, Crawford's incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture makes this a safe Republican seat with minimal competitive risk.
